rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six peaks and identify critical pairs while limiting the time penalty. The low starting organic fraction protects early retention, and the high endpoint promotes complete elution.

Injection 1 already achieves the maximum CRF, so test a shorter gradient while retaining it as the best-scoring reference. The minimum resolution of 3.98 provides substantial margin for compression, and keeping temperature and endpoints fixed isolates the slope effect.

Shorten the gradient another grid step to seek a faster method with the same maximum CRF. The first pair is slope-sensitive but still has resolution margin at tG = 6 min; keep temperature and endpoints fixed to test its limit.

The first pair is near the resolution threshold, so test temperature rather than further steepening the gradient. Raising temperature may shorten retention and improve selectivity, while injection 3 remains a verified maximum-CRF fallback.

Heating substantially worsened the critical first pair, so test the opposite temperature limit at the same gradient slope. Improved selectivity at 25 C could provide room to shorten the gradient while preserving maximum CRF.

The lower temperature improved the critical pair to R = 2.48; now test the minimum gradient duration to establish the compression limit. If resolution falls below 1.5, a narrower organic window can provide an intermediate slope without increasing tG.

Narrow the gradient by raising the starting organic fraction, making the slope shallower to recover first-pair resolution at the minimum tG. Retain the high endpoint to keep the last compound eluting promptly; the first peak’s estimated elution fraction was about 0.33 in injection 6.

Injection 7 recovered maximum CRF at the minimum gradient duration. Raise phi0 one grid step to test whether further window trimming shortens elution while retaining adequate separation of the early pair.

Use the first pair’s resolution margin to test a small temperature increase for faster elution while preserving maximum CRF. Keep the gradient fixed, since further raising phi0 risks pushing the earliest peak toward the unretained region.

Test the upper starting-organic boundary at the temperature that best separates the first pair. The narrower gradient may shorten the last retention time, but this run will establish whether early-peak compression limits further window trimming; injection 9 remains the fastest verified maximum-CRF method.

Return to phi0 = 0.30 and test the next temperature step to establish the fastest fully resolved boundary. The first pair may fall just below R = 1.5; if so, injection 9 remains the fastest verified method with maximum CRF.

Reduce the endpoint to make the gradient shallower and recover the first pair’s resolution at 35 C. The last peak may move into the final hold, but the short retention times leave ample room to preserve maximum CRF.

The first pair barely responded to lowering phi1, suggesting it elutes too early to benefit much from the gradient. Lower phi0 to increase its retention and test whether this restores full resolution at 35 C while keeping the run short.

Lower phi1 one grid step to further reduce the slope; the first pair needs only about a 6% resolution improvement to reach full credit. This tests a maximum-CRF alternative at 35 C, with some additional hold-time retention expected for the last peak.

Return to the fastest verified temperature and starting fraction, lowering phi1 one step to test a nearby maximum-CRF method with slightly more resolution margin. Injection 14 is borderline despite its rounded score, while injection 9 remains the fastest clearly fully resolved method.

Lower phi0 one step from injection 15 to move the early peaks away from the unretained region while retaining a short gradient. This tests a potentially more robust maximum-CRF alternative; injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method.

Lower temperature one step from injection 16 to improve the critical pair’s resolution while keeping early peaks adequately retained. This should provide a short, maximum-CRF alternative with more separation margin than the 30 C method.

Test a lower starting fraction with the high endpoint to retain the early peaks more strongly while keeping the last peak near 2.7 minutes. This probes the lower-phi0 boundary for full resolution at minimum gradient duration; injection 9 remains the fastest verified maximum-CRF method.

Combine the starting fraction that gave the best first-pair separation with a slightly shallower gradient at 25 C. This tests a short maximum-CRF alternative with additional resolution margin, while injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method.

Test a slightly shallower gradient at the temperature most favorable to the critical pair, with phi0 low enough to keep the first peak away from the unretained region. This seeks additional separation margin in a short maximum-CRF method; injection 9 remains the fastest verified option.

Raise temperature one step from injection 20 to shorten its final hold retention while using the first pair’s resolution margin. This should yield another fully resolved, maximum-CRF method with better early retention than the fastest verified method, injection 9.

Lower phi1 one step from injection 18 to add resolution margin to its borderline first pair while retaining the early peaks near one minute. This tests a short maximum-CRF alternative without repeating a method; injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved option.

Test one endpoint step below injection 19 to increase the critical pair’s separation margin while keeping the run well below the time-penalty threshold. Maximum CRF is already secured, and injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method.

Raise temperature one step from injection 23 to shorten the last peak’s hold retention while retaining sufficient first-pair resolution. This tests a nearby maximum-CRF alternative; injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method.

Use the final injection to test a shallower variant of injection 22, aiming to increase first-pair resolution while retaining all peaks comfortably within 10 minutes. The campaign has already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000; injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method.
